## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed and executable code like this:

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

library(tidyverse)
library(AER)

data("DoctorVisits", package = "AER")

DoctorVisits |>
  ggplot(aes(x = illness)) +
  geom_histogram(stat = "count")
```

*Figure 3.1: Number of illnesses in the past two weeks, based on the 1977-1978 Australian Health Survey*

Blank line - on either side of R chunk to run proper. Most people did not visit a doctor in the past week.

#| warning: false

# Evaluation Options

Various options available in chunks include these on new line by opening with chunk-specific comment delimiter "#\|" and then the option. Helpful options include:

echo: this controls whether the code itself is included in the document

For instance: #\| echo: false

would mean the code will be ran and its output will show, but the code itself will not be included in the document.

```{r}
#| echo: false
 
2*2

#| eval: false

2*2
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed). And then the oposite for `eval: false` ???

$$A = P\left(1+\frac{r}{n}\right)^{nt}$$

$$y_i|\mu_i, \sigma \sim \mbox{Normal}(\mu_i, \sigma)$$

$$\begin{aligned}
y_i|\pi_i & \sim \mbox{Bern}(\pi_i) \\
\mbox{logit}(\pi_i) & = \beta_0+ \alpha_{g[i]}^{\mbox{gender}} + \alpha_{a[i]}^{\mbox{age}} + \alpha_{s[i]}^{\mbox{state}} + \alpha_{e[i]}^{\mbox{edu}} \\
\beta_0 & \sim \mbox{Normal}(0, 2.5)\\
\alpha_{g}^{\mbox{gender}} & \sim \mbox{Normal}(0, 2.5)\mbox{ for }g=1, 2\\
\alpha_{a}^{\mbox{age}} & \sim \mbox{Normal}\left(0, \sigma^2_{\mbox{age}}\right)\mbox{ for }a = 1, 2, \dots, A\\
\alpha_{s}^{\mbox{state}} & \sim \mbox{Normal}\left(0, \sigma^2_{\mbox{state}}\right)\mbox{ for }s = 1, 2, \dots, S\\
\alpha_{e}^{\mbox{edu}} & \sim \mbox{Normal}\left(0, \sigma^2_{\mbox{edu}}\right)\mbox{ for }e = 1, 2, \dots, E\\
\sigma_{\mbox{gender}} & \sim \mbox{Exponential}(1)\\
\sigma_{\mbox{state}} & \sim \mbox{Exponential}(1)\\
\sigma_{\mbox{edu}} & \sim \mbox{Exponential}(1)
\end{aligned}$$

# Cross references

```{r}
#| label: fig-uniquename
#| fig-cap: Number of illnesses in the past two weeks, based on the 1977--1978 Australian Health Survey
#| warning: false

data("DoctorVisits", package = "AER")

DoctorVisits |>
  ggplot(aes(x = illness)) +
  geom_histogram(stat = "count") 
```

*Figure 3.3: Number of illnesses in the past two weeks, based on the 1977-1978 Australian Health Survey*


```{r}
#Add #| layout-ncol: 2 in an R chunk to have two graphs appear side by side (Figure 3.4a and 3.4b), where one uses minimal and one uses classic theme. 

#| eval: true
#| warning: false
#| label: fig-doctorgraphsidebyside
#| fig-cap: "Two variants of graphs"
#| fig-subcap: ["Illnesses","Visits to the doctor"]
#| layout-ncol: 2

DoctorVisits |>
  ggplot(aes(x = illness)) +
  geom_histogram(stat = "count") +
  theme_minimal()

DoctorVisits |>
  ggplot(aes(x = visits)) +
  geom_histogram(stat = "count") +
  theme_classic()

#These both cross reference the same label [#| fig-doctorgraphsidebyside] in the R chunk with option added for subcaptions

```

```{r}
#Similar approach to cross-reference tables!

#| label: tbl-docvisittable
#| tbl-cap: "Distribution of the number of doctor visits"

library(knitr)

DoctorVisits |>
  count(visits) |>
  kable()
```
